title: Faithful homomorphisms of affine algebraic groups are closed immersions
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $G,H$ be affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$. Let $f:G\to H$ be a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes. Suppose that for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ the group homomorphism $f_R:G(R)\to H(R)$ is injective, where $G(R)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}R,G)$ and likewise for $H$. Then $f$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. No smoothness, connectedness or perfectness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 3.35, printed p.75, with Theorem 3.34 on the same page: injectivity on all algebra points is the trivial scheme-theoretic kernel condition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] to the given homomorphism. It gives an affine finite-type $k$-group scheme $I$ and homomorphisms $u:G\to I$, $j:I\to H$ with $f=j\circ u$, $j$ a closed immersion, and $k[G]$ faithfully flat over $k[I]$. The hypotheses are exactly those assumed here, with no smoothness or reducedness condition. For every $k$-algebra $R$, $u_R(a)=u_R(b)$ implies $f_R(a)=j_Ru_R(a)=j_Ru_R(b)=f_R(b)$, hence $a=b$ by the hypothesis. Thus $u_R$ is injective for every such $R$.

source.place: Corollary 3.35, printed p.75, first two sentences; Theorem 3.34 on the same page.

proof.text: The map $u$ is an fpqc covering. Indeed, put $A=k[I]$, $B=k[G]$ and identify $u$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(u^*:A\to B)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Faithful flatness implies flatness by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]; [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] therefore makes $u$ a flat morphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum], $u$ is surjective on underlying spaces. Also [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] says that for every affine open $V\subset I$, the open $u^{-1}(V)\subset G$ is affine. Its image is all of $V$ by surjectivity. Taking this single affine open for each $V$ gives exactly the finite refinement required in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], so $\{u:G\to I\}$ is an fpqc covering.

source.place: Corollary 3.35, printed p.75, faithfully flat descent diagram. The covering hypotheses are expanded using Stacks Tags 01U5 (morphisms-lemma-flat-characterize), 00HQ (algebra-lemma-ff-rings), 01SH (morphisms-lemma-morphism-affines-affine) and 022B (topologies-definition-fpqc-covering).

proof.text: Form $P=G\times_I G$ with projections $p_1,p_2:P\to G$ [def-pc-fibre-product], so $u\circ p_1=u\circ p_2$. Since $u$ is affine by step 2, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1) makes $P\to G$ affine, and (2), since $G$ is affine, makes $P$ affine. Write $P=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with its induced $k$-algebra structure [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Both projections are $k$-morphisms, hence points of $G(C)$. Their images under $u_C$ agree by the fibre-product equation; step 1's injectivity for this very $k$-algebra $C$ gives $p_1=p_2$. Thus $\mathrm{id}_G\circ p_1=\mathrm{id}_G\circ p_2$, the required descent compatibility.

source.place: Corollary 3.35, printed p.75, diagram chase: agreement of the two pullbacks of a lift. Affineness of the overlap uses Stacks Tags 01SD (morphisms-lemma-base-change-affine) and 01S6 (morphisms-definition-affine).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to the covering $u:G\to I$, target $G$, and local map $\mathrm{id}_G$. Step 3 verifies its overlap hypothesis, so it gives a scheme morphism $s:I\to G$ with $s\circ u=\mathrm{id}_G$. Now $(u\circ s)\circ u=u=\mathrm{id}_I\circ u$. Apply the uniqueness clause of the same descent statement with target $I$ and local map $u$: both $u\circ s$ and $\mathrm{id}_I$ descend that map, hence $u\circ s=\mathrm{id}_I$. Therefore $u$ is an isomorphism with inverse $s$. This constructs the inverse as a morphism, rather than inferring it from bijectivity of field-valued points.

source.place: Corollary 3.35, printed p.75, final diagram chase, expressed by descending the universal lift; Stacks Tag 023Q (descent-lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms).

proof.text: For each affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}D\subset H$, the closed-immersion criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion] for $j$ identifies $j^{-1}(V)$ over $V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(D/J)$ for an ideal $J\subset D$. Since $u$ is an isomorphism and $f=j\circ u$, its restriction identifies $f^{-1}(V)$ over $V$ with this same $\operatorname{Spec}(D/J)$. The criterion therefore shows that $f$ is a closed immersion. No step required any smoothness, connectedness or perfectness hypothesis.

source.place: Corollary 3.35, printed p.75, conclusion after the faithfully flat factor is shown to be an isomorphism; affine closed-immersion criterion Stacks Tag 01QO.

proof_origin.place: Corollary 3.35 and Theorem 3.34, printed p.75. The fpqc diagram chase is performed on the universal point using Stacks Tag 023Q; the fpqc covering is checked with Tags 01U5, 00HQ, 01SH and 022B.
